import pandas as pd

def main():
    # File paths for sources and target
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_56/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_56/test_1.csv"
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_56/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Load Source 0
    # Schema: ['calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name', 'calaccess_filing_id', 'date_received',
    #          'contributor_lastname', 'contributor_firstname', 'contributor_city', 'contributor_state',
    #          'contributor_zip', 'contributor_employer', 'contributor_occupation',
    #          'contributor_is_self_employed', 'amount']
    df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, dtype={
        'calaccess_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'committee_name': 'string',
        'calaccess_filing_id': 'Int64',
        'date_received': 'string',
        'contributor_lastname': 'string',
        'contributor_firstname': 'string',
        'contributor_city': 'string',
        'contributor_state': 'string',
        'contributor_zip': 'string',
        'contributor_employer': 'string',
        'contributor_occupation': 'string',
        'contributor_is_self_employed': 'boolean',
        'amount': 'float'
    })

    # Load Source 1
    # Schema: ['ocd_prop_id', 'calaccess_prop_id', 'ccdc_prop_id', 'prop_name',
    #          'ccdc_committee_id', 'calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name', 'committee_position']
    df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, dtype={
        'ocd_prop_id': 'string',
        'calaccess_prop_id': 'Int64',
        'ccdc_prop_id': 'Int64',
        'prop_name': 'string',
        'ccdc_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'calaccess_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'committee_name': 'string',
        'committee_position': 'string'
    })

    # --- Transformation Plan ---
    # Goal: Produce Target1_56 with schema:
    # ['ocd_prop_id': string, 'calaccess_prop_id': integer, 'ccdc_prop_id': integer, 'prop_name': string,
    #  'ccdc_committee_id': integer, 'calaccess_committee_id': integer, 'committee_name_x': string,
    #  'committee_position': string, 'committee_name_y': string, 'calaccess_filing_id': integer,
    #  'date_received': string, 'contributor_lastname': string, 'contributor_firstname': string,
    #  'contributor_city': string, 'contributor_state': string, 'contributor_zip': string,
    #  'contributor_employer': string, 'contributor_occupation': string, 'contributor_is_self_employed': boolean,
    #  'amount': float]

    # Source 0 has detailed contributor and filing info but no prop info.
    # Source 1 has prop info and committee position but no contributor/filer info.

    # Join key candidates:
    # - committee_name (high overlap)
    # - calaccess_committee_id (numeric id)
    # Because committee_name is not unique in either source, and calaccess_committee_id is repeated,
    # we will join on both calaccess_committee_id and committee_name to reduce ambiguity.

    # However, previous attempts failed due to non-unique keys on right side.
    # To handle this, we will:
    # 1. Aggregate Source 1 by calaccess_committee_id and committee_name to keep unique rows per committee-position-prop.
    #    But since committee_position and prop info are needed, we keep all rows.
    # 2. Join Source 0 with Source 1 on ['calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name'] with a many-to-many join.
    # 3. This will produce a larger dataframe with all combinations.
    # 4. Rename columns accordingly.

    # To avoid explosion, we trust the data is manageable.

    # Rename Source 0 committee_name to committee_name_y (to match target)
    df0 = df0.rename(columns={'committee_name': 'committee_name_y'})

    # Rename Source 1 committee_name to committee_name_x (to match target)
    df1 = df1.rename(columns={'committee_name': 'committee_name_x'})

    # Merge on calaccess_committee_id and committee_name (committee_name_x from df1, committee_name_y from df0)
    # Because names differ, join on calaccess_committee_id and committee_name_x == committee_name_y
    merged = pd.merge(
        df1,
        df0,
        left_on=['calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name_x'],
        right_on=['calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name_y'],
        how='inner',
        suffixes=('_x', '_y')
    )

    # Select and reorder columns to match target schema
    # Target schema:
    # ['ocd_prop_id', 'calaccess_prop_id', 'ccdc_prop_id', 'prop_name',
    #  'ccdc_committee_id', 'calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name_x',
    #  'committee_position', 'committee_name_y', 'calaccess_filing_id',
    #  'date_received', 'contributor_lastname', 'contributor_firstname',
    #  'contributor_city', 'contributor_state', 'contributor_zip',
    #  'contributor_employer', 'contributor_occupation', 'contributor_is_self_employed',
    #  'amount']

    target_columns = [
        'ocd_prop_id',
        'calaccess_prop_id',
        'ccdc_prop_id',
        'prop_name',
        'ccdc_committee_id',
        'calaccess_committee_id',
        'committee_name_x',
        'committee_position',
        'committee_name_y',
        'calaccess_filing_id',
        'date_received',
        'contributor_lastname',
        'contributor_firstname',
        'contributor_city',
        'contributor_state',
        'contributor_zip',
        'contributor_employer',
        'contributor_occupation',
        'contributor_is_self_employed',
        'amount'
    ]

    # Check if all columns exist in merged
    missing_cols = [col for col in target_columns if col not in merged.columns]
    if missing_cols:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing columns after merge: {missing_cols}")

    df_target = merged[target_columns]

    # Enforce dtypes as per target schema
    df_target = df_target.astype({
        'ocd_prop_id': 'string',
        'calaccess_prop_id': 'Int64',
        'ccdc_prop_id': 'Int64',
        'prop_name': 'string',
        'ccdc_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'calaccess_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'committee_name_x': 'string',
        'committee_position': 'string',
        'committee_name_y': 'string',
        'calaccess_filing_id': 'Int64',
        'date_received': 'string',
        'contributor_lastname': 'string',
        'contributor_firstname': 'string',
        'contributor_city': 'string',
        'contributor_state': 'string',
        'contributor_zip': 'string',
        'contributor_employer': 'string',
        'contributor_occupation': 'string',
        'contributor_is_self_employed': 'boolean',
        'amount': 'float'
    })

    # Write to CSV
    df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
